title: India Rout Japan 49-24 to Open Kabaddi Title Defence at Asian Games
excerpt: Ashu Malik's three-point Super Raid set the tone as debutants starred in a dominant opening group-stage win at Nagoya's Tokai Citizens Gymnasium.
body:
• Defending champions India opened their men's kabaddi title defence at the Asian Games 2026 with a 49-24 win over hosts Japan on Monday.
  • Asian Games debutants Ashu Malik, Ayan Lohchab and Devank Dalal led the attack; Malik's three-point Super Raid set the tone early.
  • India led 31-9 at half-time after three all-outs in the opening 20 minutes, and never looked threatened at the Tokai Citizens Gymnasium in Nagoya.
  • India play South Korea in their second group match on Tuesday; the top two teams from each group advance to the semifinals.

India's men's kabaddi team launched their Asian Games title defence in dominant fashion on Monday, hammering hosts Japan 49-24 in their opening group match at the Tokai Citizens Gymnasium in Aichi Prefecture, Nagoya.

The defending champions were never truly tested. After Japan opened the scoring with a bonus point, Ayan Lohchab levelled with a touch point, and India seized control from there — racing to an 18-2 lead after two early all-outs and taking a 31-9 advantage into half-time.

How the match unfolded

The tone was set by raider Ashu Malik, whose superb three-point Super Raid helped India inflict their first all-out and establish an 11-2 lead. A second all-out followed quickly to make it 18-2, and by the 20-minute mark India had inflicted three all-outs on the hosts, building a commanding 31-9 half-time lead.

Japan's scoring was largely restricted to bonus points, as India's defence denied the hosts any sustained raiding momentum. Shortly after the restart, India pushed Japan to a fourth all-out and extended the lead to 40-12. Japan rallied in the closing stages and outscored India from that point to trim the margin, but the outcome was never in doubt.

The debutants deliver

Asian Games debutants Ayan Lohchab, Devank Dalal and Ashu Malik were India's most impactful attackers, with Malik leading the raid unit. In defence, Rahul Sethpal was disciplined throughout, keeping Japan's raiding options in check, with Sunil Kumar contributing strongly. After the break, Pawan Sehrawat, Arjun Deshwal and Aslam Inamdar joined the action and added to India's attacking strength.

The blend of new faces and established names is the story of this squad. As The Videshi reported earlier, India arrived in Nagoya with a new-generation team tasked with defending the title — and the opener suggested the transition is in capable hands.

The weight of history

India are by far the most successful team in Asian Games kabaddi history, with 11 golds from the 13 titles on offer. The men have won eight of nine editions — the only blemish being the bronze at Jakarta 2018 — while the women have won three of four, with a silver in 2018. Japan's best Asian Games finish remains the men's bronze at Guangzhou 2010.

Monday's result underlined the gulf, but the group stage is only the beginning. India face South Korea in their second group match on Tuesday, with the top two teams from each group progressing to the semifinals.

What's next

The South Korea match on Tuesday offers a sterner test before the knockout rounds. For now, India have done exactly what defending champions are supposed to do in an opener: win big, rotate the squad, and send an early message to the rest of the field.
